text:
deploybot: Scheduled rollout v2.4.1 -> us-east-1 canary queueing in 10m: https://deploys/release/2.4.1

kai: FYI getting a spike of 500s from model-service in us-east since ~5m ago. Pager fired.

rebecca: Confirmed — multiple pod restarts, logs show OOMs in kvcache alloc.

emily_r: Can we pause the canary? I'm mid-change-window and don't want to overlap with this incident.

deploybot: Canary start automatically PAUSED by ops flag: incident/model-service-5xx. Reason: ongoing SRE incident.

ben_s: Thank you. Quick proposal: hold this release, pin traffic to v2.4.0 where cached KVs are stable, and reschedule canary to tomorrow 09:00 PT. Thoughts?

sara_ops: +1 to holding. Ops needs time to validate patch for kvcache bounds. If we pin, we should also lock the schema-migration flag in the release config.

samir: If we pin, we need to ensure Dedicated customers on reserved pools aren't affected. I'll check routing policies.

rebecca: Patch candidate ready in ci: kvcache/fix-bounds-9. Would reduce memory peak. We should validate on a staging canary before requeue.

emily_r: Action items: 1) Hold v2.4.1 rollout (ben) 2) Patch and smoke test kvcache/fix-bounds-9 in staging (rebecca) 3) Validate routing for dedicated pools (samir) 4) Update release notes & change window (me) 5) Communicate to support and customers (sara).

ben_s: I've applied a temporary version pin on the rollout: pinned v2.4.0 -> all canary slots now locked. Command used: `deployctl pin --release release-2.4 --version 2.4.0 --scope canary`

deploybot: Pin acknowledged. Rollout state: PAUSED (pinned).

kai: SRE will continue incident work. ETA for initial mitigation attempt: 1h. I'll post updates.

rebecca: I'll run the patch pipeline now and post smoke logs.

samir: Routing check: dedicated pools unaffected, but we saw 2 internal routes that would have preferred v2.4.1. I've set them to fallback-to-stable.

emily_r: For scheduling — moving the canary to tomorrow 09:00 PT. Anyone object?

sara_ops: No objections. Ops prefers 09:00 PT. Also request a shorter blast radius: start with 1% traffic for 30m, then ramp manually.

ben_s: Noted. Will update the release calendar and add the manual ramp step.

rebecca: Staging smoke looks good so far (no OOMs in 30m). Will run an additional 2-hour soak test and post results.

kai: Incident update: mitigation reduced 5xx by 60%. Root cause points to an unexpected token growth pattern under specific prefix workloads. Still validating.

emily_r: I'll draft a short customer-facing blurb about the delay and expected new window, and post to #customer-communications once approved.

ben_s: I've updated the release doc: https://docs/releases/2.4.1 - added pin justification, new window, and rollout checklist.

samir: Routing reverted for dedicated pools to original fallback-after-60s once we confirm staging soak.

sara_ops: Support notified, created internal KB: "v2.4.1 hold due to model-service kvcache OOMs". Tagging priority customers that had canaries scheduled.

rebecca: Soak complete, logs attached. No regressions observed on staging.

kai: SRE sign-off pending final metrics pass in 20m. If clean, we can greenlight a controlled requeue. But prefer waiting until morning per ops.

emily_r: Ok we keep the hold overnight. Final checklist before reschedule: - confirm patch merged & builds green - update release notes - ensure manual ramp steps present - ops SLA contact included in rollout ticket.

ben_s: Done, all checklist items updated. I'll unpin and requeue tomorrow after ops ACK.

deploybot: Thread closed by pause flag; will resume when `ops:requeue` message is posted.

sara_ops: Thanks everyone. Please add any follow-ups if I missed them. :thumbsup:

kai: Noted, will post final incident summary when available.
